draft.title: PINES Management Processes — Consolidated Reporting & Tools Requirements (Final Draft)
draft.scope: Requirements for management reporting, analysis, and collection/asset-management utilities used by PINES library managers, administrators, and staff. This covers reporting features, query tools and templates, item transfer and purging utilities, deletion/audit logging, patron-demographic and inactivity reporting, reporting infrastructure (performance, queueing, scheduling, historical data), platform and security constraints, documentation and help, and related operational processes. It explicitly excludes day-to-day patron-facing OPAC and circulation client functional requirements except where those systems are a required data source.
glossary: OPAC: Online Public Access Catalog (public-facing catalog interface).
Report template / canned report: A pre-configured query and display format that staff may run or modify subject to permissions.
Data warehouse / reporting warehouse: A copy or aggregation layer of production data optimized for historical reporting and snapshot queries.
Pull list / transit label: Printed output to assist physical movement of items (barcodes, destination, etc.).
Reversion / auto-revert: Automatic process that returns an item's location (or location field) to a previous value after a configured condition or time interval.
Snapshot report: A saved (time-stamped) result set for historical comparison that does not change when live data changes.
Last copy report: Report identifying bibliographic records for which a system or branch holds the last known copy.
Denormalized schema: A database schema arranged to speed reporting at the cost of duplication; discouraged unless specifically justified.

requirements.name: Material Volume Reporting
requirements.explanation: The system shall provide reports showing the volume of material in the library at a given point in time and over time. Reports shall include counts of new acquisitions, items on shelf (checked in), and items out in circulation. Reports shall allow breaking down volume by categories (for example: total items, number of holds, adult fiction, board books) and shall support customizable categories and historical/time-based summaries.
requirements.priority_reason: Explicit request and central management need for collection volume and categorization; core management process requirement.

requirements.name: Branch Capacity Overview and Drill-Down
requirements.explanation: The system shall provide a high-level summary (dashboard) view that displays capacity metrics for all branches simultaneously. Users shall be able to drill down from the multi-branch overview to detailed capacity information for an individual branch. The dashboard shall support sorting and filtering (e.g., by region, library type, current load) and display trends indicating whether branches are growing or shrinking over time to aid long-term planning.
requirements.priority_reason: Explicitly requested as a core executive/managerial view and referenced as 'must' for decision making.

requirements.name: Shelf Space Utilization and Comparative Reporting
requirements.explanation: The system shall provide a shelf-space report that, for each genre and format, computes and compares: percentage of total circulations, percentage of the collection, and percentage of total shelf space. The report shall be runnable per library and at the system level, allow side-by-side comparisons across libraries (comparison view), and support date-range filtering to compare quarters or seasons. Because shelf space is not directly tracked, the system shall provide an estimation method (see separate requirement) and document estimation assumptions in the report output.
requirements.priority_reason: Multiple stakeholders requested this report for collection management and system comparison; functionality is specifically described and required.

requirements.name: Shelf Space Estimation Investigations
requirements.explanation: Because shelf space is not tracked directly, the project shall investigate and document methods to estimate shelf space from existing data (for example, using item dimensions if available, or using item count as a proxy). The selected estimation approach and its limitations shall be recorded and surfaced in the shelf-space report so users understand assumptions and accuracy.
requirements.priority_reason: Estimation is necessary for the shelf-space report to be usable, but approaches may vary; investigation and documented method are required though choice of algorithm is implementation detail.

requirements.name: Export and Report Output Formats (CSV/Pivot/Fields)
requirements.explanation: The system shall allow exporting reports and report results in common formats such as CSV for spreadsheet use, and support pivot-table-ready output. Reports shall be able to include multiple output columns (e.g., last month's circulation, previous month's circulation, percent differences, previous year's month) and be able to include MARC fields or other bibliographic fields so that relevant bibliographic data can appear on a single row per result when requested.
requirements.priority_reason: Export to CSV and flexible output columns are repeatedly requested for directors and staff who work with spreadsheets; fundamental for interoperability.

requirements.name: Shelf / Transfer Physical Handling Outputs (Pull Lists & Labels)
requirements.explanation: When items are selected for transfer or movement, the system shall be able to produce printable pull lists and transit labels that include barcodes and destination information to streamline physical handling and tracking. Pull lists shall be printable and exportable for staff workflows.
requirements.priority_reason: Physical handling of transferred items requires printed lists/labels to operationalize transfers.

requirements.name: Item Transfer / Branch Transfer Utility
requirements.explanation: The system shall provide a transfer utility supporting: a query builder to select candidate items for transfer (with ability to save/share queries as templates), manual selection (checkboxes) from query results, changing selected items' location fields (batch update) or producing pull lists for physical transfer, and a mechanism to revert items to their original location (automatic or manual) after a configured period or upon certain events. The utility shall have permissions restricting who may perform transfers and must support preview and confirmation before changes, an undo/rollback mechanism, notifications for transfer delays or issues, and logging of transfer activities for audit purposes.
requirements.priority_reason: Staff operational need for predictable, repeatable transfers and safeguards (preview, undo, permissions) is strongly emphasized; transfers affect large numbers of items and must be controlled.

requirements.name: Auto-Revert and Scheduled Reversion Processing
requirements.explanation: The system shall support automatic reversion of transferred items to their original location based on elapsed time (configurable, e.g., 30 days) and/or event triggers (e.g., status change to 'sold', item checked out at destination). A background scheduled task shall periodically evaluate transferred items and perform reversion or flag items for review according to configured criteria.
requirements.priority_reason: Auto-revert automates maintenance but policies and exact triggers need local configuration; listed as important but implementation details configurable.

requirements.name: Transfer Activity Logging and Item Transfer History
requirements.explanation: All transfer-related activities (batch updates, manual transfers, reverts, pull-list generation, and notifications) shall be logged. The system shall allow viewing the transfer history for an individual item (for example, number of transfers in the past year) to identify circulation or location issues.
requirements.priority_reason: Operational traceability and auditing are essential for trustworthy inventory operations and to diagnose transfer-related problems.

requirements.name: Permissions and Role Restrictions for Transfer & Report Actions
requirements.explanation: The system shall restrict transfer, purge, and other data-modifying functions to authorized roles (e.g., managers, administrators, transfer coordinators). Permissions shall be manageable via roles and security groups so that altering a user's role updates their permissions automatically.
requirements.priority_reason: Prevents unauthorized or accidental data modifications; explicitly requested.

requirements.name: Missing, Damaged, and In-Transit Items Reporting
requirements.explanation: The system shall generate reports listing missing and damaged items, segmented by branch. The system shall also provide an in-transit items report that lists items in transit beyond a configurable number of days (default configurable; a suggested default is 7 days), merging outbound and inbound transit records into one view, and support sorting (for example by due date) to prioritize action.
requirements.priority_reason: Regular shelf-reading and transit monitoring require actionable reports; repeatedly requested by cataloging and operations staff.

requirements.name: Item Purging / Weeding Utility and Safety Controls
requirements.explanation: The system shall provide a utility and reports to identify candidate item records for purging using configurable combined criteria (e.g., status='missing' for > X months, status='discard/weed', circulation inactivity). Workflows shall include read-only candidate reports, a separate confirmation step before deletion, last-copy reports to avoid deleting sole copies, and an audit trail of purge actions. There shall also be tools for deleting volume entries along with their copies and cleaning records with no attached items.
requirements.priority_reason: Data removal is sensitive and requires safe workflows and auditability; explicitly requested by cataloging and operations staff.

requirements.name: Deletion Audit Logging and Deletion Report Interface
requirements.explanation: The system shall log deletions (records removed) to an audit table capturing at a minimum: record_type, record_id, deleted_by, deleted_at (timestamp), and location. The system shall provide a report interface to query the audit table and allow filtering by date range, user, record type, location, and system. The system shall also count deletions by period (monthly/quarterly/yearly) and by record type and location, and shall log attempted/denied deletions for security monitoring. The capability to list deleted items that were last copies (for updating external catalogs such as WorldCat) shall be supported.
requirements.priority_reason: Deletion logging does not exist in current system and is necessary for auditability, compliance, and troubleshooting; explicitly requested.

requirements.name: Query Builder and Report Designer UI
requirements.explanation: The system shall provide a user-friendly query-builder interface for designing complex queries across all record types. Features shall include selecting fields, picklist value selection, regular-expression support, Boolean operators, visible display of query criteria alongside results, and the ability to save/share queries and create report templates that administrators can make available to staff (runnable as-is or editable within admin-defined constraints). Templates shall be clonable to create variants.
requirements.priority_reason: Core functionality for staff to define ad-hoc and recurring reports; consistently emphasized across stakeholders.

requirements.name: Report Templates, Shared Folders and Fine-Grained Report Permissions
requirements.explanation: The system shall support administrator-created report templates, shared folders for report access control, and fine-grained permissions to control who may create, clone, edit, run, schedule, or distribute reports. Permissions shall reflect role changes dynamically and support folders or collections of templates with controlled editability. Administrators shall be able to limit which filters and display fields staff may alter.
requirements.priority_reason: Consistency and security in reporting across the consortium require template management and permission controls; explicit user requests and surveys indicate this as necessary.

requirements.name: Report Scheduling, Queue Management, Prioritization and Cancellation
requirements.explanation: The system shall provide a queuing mechanism for report processing, show users their report position in the queue (number of reports ahead, submission time, current status such as waiting/running/completed/failed), allow cancelling scheduled or running reports, and allow prioritization/escalation of reports (for example, giving board reports priority over ad-hoc staff reports). The system shall permit scheduling frequencies including Run ASAP, Hourly, Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Yearly and support email delivery and address-book based distribution.
requirements.priority_reason: Operationally necessary to manage heavy reporting load and to ensure critical reports are delivered timely; explicitly requested.

requirements.name: Historical Reporting and Data Warehouse Support
requirements.explanation: The system shall support historical reporting via a reporting warehouse or snapshot capability that allows acquiring data as-of a given date or date range and generating snapshot reports for longitudinal analysis. Transaction history retention shall be configurable (X days), while monthly and annual aggregates shall be retained indefinitely if configured. The reporting architecture shall avoid denormalized schemas that cause sync issues unless a justified ETL approach is chosen.
requirements.priority_reason: Historical analysis is valuable for planning and required by some users; implementation may require architectural work so priority is 'Should' where not explicitly called 'must' though many stakeholders requested it.

requirements.name: Background Processing, Read-Only Reporting Replicas and Performance
requirements.explanation: To avoid disrupting live circulation and OPAC performance during open hours, the system shall support running long queries and reports as background jobs, caching results, using queuing, and/or using read-only reporting replicas. The system shall scale to support a large consortium (for example, 286 locations, ~17M annual circulations, and ~900k items/year processed) without adversely affecting online patrons and staff operations.
requirements.priority_reason: Large-consortium scale and explicit reports of current system contention make background processing/read-only replicas essential for operational viability.

requirements.name: Server Platform, Browser and Accessibility Requirements
requirements.explanation: Management Processes shall operate on Linux or Solaris server environments. If web-browser access is used, the system shall be accessible through Microsoft Internet Explorer (v6.0 and later) and Mozilla Firefox (v2.0 and later). The system shall produce standards-compliant HTML and support assistive technologies (screen-reading, screen-magnification), complying with accessibility requirements (e.g., Section 508).
requirements.priority_reason: Explicit platform & accessibility constraints were stated as high priority and/or legal/regulatory requirements.

requirements.name: Authentication Options and Individual Auditability
requirements.explanation: The system shall support multiple staff login methods including streamlined local login (e.g., card-swipe) and traditional username/password. Streamlined login shall still identify the specific staff member for audit purposes, and role-based access control shall be used so that changing a user's role updates their permissions automatically.
requirements.priority_reason: Multiple login options aid usability; individual auditability is essential but the streamlined option can be optional per site.

requirements.name: Help System and Error Reporting
requirements.explanation: The system shall provide an integrated online help system in HTML that is hierarchical, cross-linked, searchable, and illustrates all major functions. The system shall also provide high-level error reporting and low-level query-specific feedback for administrators to support troubleshooting.
requirements.priority_reason: Users require integrated help and administrators require diagnostics for effective operation; marked High Priority in source material.

requirements.name: Data Specification and Major Process Documentation
requirements.explanation: The developer shall provide complete data specifications for authority, bibliographic, order, item, hold/request, and other records used by Management Processes. The developer shall also provide high-level descriptions of major processes (e.g., bibliographic import/export, validation, reporting processes) so staff and developers understand data structures and flows used by reports.
requirements.priority_reason: Report authors, administrators, and integrators require accurate data specification and process descriptions to build and validate reports.

requirements.name: Transaction-level Reporting and Counting
requirements.explanation: The system shall support transaction reporting grouped by hour, terminal, branch, and system. It shall count separately and cumulatively all check-in and check-out types (e.g., book-drop, staff, self-checkout, renewals via staff and OPAC). Holds reporting shall include method of placement (staff desk, public computer, remote), and transaction reports shall support per-patron, per-library, per-group-of-libraries, per-system, and per-county rollups. Reports shall include total circulations broken down by checkouts, renewals, and non-cataloged uses where applicable.
requirements.priority_reason: Detailed transaction accounting and breakdowns are core reporting needs described repeatedly in source material.

requirements.name: Patron Demographics, Filtering, Grouping and Inactive Patron Reports
requirements.explanation: The system shall support filtering (LIMIT) and grouping (GROUP BY) of patron records by characteristics such as zip code, county, home branch, patron type, preferred language, and effective age range. Age ranges shall be computed at query time from birth_date and be configurable. Filters shall be combinable with AND/OR logic, and reports shall include null/missing values rather than silently excluding them. Inactivity reports shall allow a configurable inactivity threshold (X days, default commonly 365), include electronic activity (OPAC logins, online holds, renewals, digital access where logged) by combining events across tables, support excluding certain patrons (do-not-disturb, VIPs, staff, opted-out patrons), include current mailing addresses for outreach, support export (e.g., CSV), and be runnable at multiple organizational levels (system, home library, county). For very large patron datasets, inactivity reporting shall be performed as background jobs with cached results.
requirements.priority_reason: Patron segmentation and inactivity workflows are operational necessities and appear in multiple sources; performance concerns require background processing.

requirements.name: Report Metadata, Selection Criteria and Inclusion of Nulls
requirements.explanation: Each report shall clearly define and display its selection criteria and the date range applied. Reports shall include nulls and blank fields in result sets rather than silently excluding them so analysts are aware of missing data.
requirements.priority_reason: Clarity of report parameters and inclusion of nulls is needed to avoid misleading analyses; explicitly requested.

requirements.name: Valuation and Financial-style Item Reports
requirements.explanation: The system shall provide reports that compute the monetary value of items based on data in item records (value of entire collection or subsets, e.g., all items with status 'longoverdue', or all DVDs in children's collection). Reports shall be filterable by status and media type and comply with accounting/audit requirements.
requirements.priority_reason: Valuation reports are important for financial and insurance needs but are less frequently requested than operational reports; still required and must comply with auditing standards.

requirements.name: Data Quality, Inventory and Uncataloged Material Tracking
requirements.explanation: The system shall include data-quality reports to identify inconsistencies such as invalid item types, bibliographic records with no items, long call numbers, and other anomalies. The system shall support tracking uncataloged material (e.g., large shipments of paperbacks or children's books) to enable quick distribution with minimal branch labor and to monitor usage and circulation of uncataloged items. Reports shall show last edit dates where items were explicitly modified (not last circulation date) when that information is available.
requirements.priority_reason: Data quality and uncataloged-material tracking are important for operations and efficiency; prioritized but some sites may treat as lower immediate priority than core reporting.

requirements.name: Pull MARC Fields, Last-Copy and Deleted Items Reporting for External Catalogs
requirements.explanation: The system shall be able to include MARC record fields in report rows and produce reports identifying items deleted that were last copies held by the facility to support updates to external catalogs (e.g., WorldCat).
requirements.priority_reason: Maintaining bibliographic data in external systems and producing single-row MARC outputs are explicit operational needs.

requirements.name: Report Development Process, Prototyping, and Working Group Responsibilities
requirements.explanation: The Reports Working Group shall document the desired reporting functionality, collect requirements via interviews, adopt/adapt existing SRS materials (e.g., Galecia King County SRS) as a foundation, and serve as the designated testing group for new reports development. UI specifics will be developed iteratively using prototypes, with an emphasis on readable documentation for technical and non-technical stakeholders.
requirements.priority_reason: Process and governance are necessary for high-quality outcomes; implementation is organizational rather than technical.

requirements.name: Scope: Management Processes Only (Separation from OPAC/Circulation Features)
requirements.explanation: The requirements in this specification shall be scoped to Management Processes (reports and analysis tools used by managers, administrators, and staff for planning, evaluation and oversight). They shall not be used to constrain the OPAC or circulation client functionality. The management reporting system shall integrate with OPAC/circulation data sources but remain operationally independent so that reporting activity does not degrade patron-facing modules.
requirements.priority_reason: Explicit scope decision by stakeholders; necessary to preserve module independence and performance.

requirements.name: Development / Training Environments and Configuration Migration
requirements.explanation: The system shall provide separate development/training environments where reports and configurations may be developed and tested without affecting production. There shall be a mechanism to migrate report templates, permission settings, and other configurations from development/training to production.
requirements.priority_reason: Separation of environments is important for safe development; stated in subcommittee and admin feedback as required but may be implemented after core features.

requirements.name: Report Queue Visibility and Management for Users
requirements.explanation: Users shall be able to view the status of their reports in the queue (position, status, submission time, estimated completion) and be able to cancel their scheduled or running reports. The system shall provide administrative controls to prioritize or escalate reports as required.
requirements.priority_reason: Operational transparency and control are necessary to manage heavy load and to provide predictable service levels.

requirements.name: Queue Prioritization Mechanism & Policy
requirements.explanation: The system shall provide mechanisms to prioritize certain classes of reports (for example, board reports) so they may jump ahead of resource-consuming ad-hoc queries. The system shall support administrative controls and an auditable prioritization policy. Policy details (limits, quotas, and escalation rules) shall be defined by stakeholders and captured as configuration.
requirements.priority_reason: Operational need to ensure critical reports are delivered timely and to manage resource contention.

requirements.name: Report Output Quality and Proven Correctness
requirements.explanation: All report outputs shall be tested and proven correct. The system shall include testable output validation and provide provenance metadata (selection criteria, query used, run time) alongside report results to support verification and reproducibility.
requirements.priority_reason: Trusted reporting requires reliable outputs and verification procedures; repeatedly requested.

requirements.name: Scheduling, Delivery and Distribution Features
requirements.explanation: The system shall support scheduling reports at granular frequencies (Run ASAP, Hourly, Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Yearly), shall support email delivery and address-book based report distribution, and shall allow editing recurring reports (changing selections and recipient addresses).
requirements.priority_reason: Operationally needed for recurring reporting and distribution to stakeholders.

requirements.name: Pivot and Advanced Output Formats
requirements.explanation: Reports shall support output formats suitable for pivoting and further analysis (pivot table export), and the system shall support common formats such as CSV, and optionally Excel/PDF per stakeholder needs.
requirements.priority_reason: Pivot-ready output and additional formats are highly useful; CSV is required and others are desirable based on stakeholder preference.

blacklist.name: Unassigned / Clarification Required Candidates
blacklist.reason: These candidates were present in the supplied corpus but were not explicitly assigned to a logical requirement in the consolidated draft above. They require clarification, consolidation, or were duplicates of content covered elsewhere. They are retained here so stakeholders can decide whether to (a) fold them into existing requirements, (b) convert them into new discrete requirements, or (c) mark them irrelevant. Several are low-clarity, repeated, or implementation-detail-only candidates. Where a candidate appears to conflict with a Must-level requirement, it is flagged for resolution rather than silently dropped.

open_questions: Shelf-space estimation: which estimation algorithm should be adopted (item dimensions where available, per-format average widths, or item-count proxy)? Provide preferred default and acceptable accuracy bounds.
Auto-revert policy specifics: what default time period should be used (suggested examples: 30 days or 90 days), and which event triggers should force immediate reversion vs. manual review?

Retention and transaction-history window: what is the default configurable 'X days' for transaction history and for how long should detailed transaction rows be retained before aggregation to monthly/annual?
Queue prioritization policy: what formal rules determine when a director's board report may jump ahead of staff queries? Should there be a limited number of priority escalations per time window?

Reporting environment architecture: will the project adopt a read-only reporting replica, an ETL-fed reporting warehouse, or a mixed approach (live background jobs with caching)? Each has different cost, latency, and consistency tradeoffs.
Export formats: beyond CSV and pivot-ready output, are there additional required export formats (e.g., Excel native, PDF for board reports)?
Electronic activity inclusion for inactivity reports: which external digital platforms (if any) must be included and which of those produce logs that the reporting system can reliably query?

Accessibility compliance target: confirm whether legacy browser versions (IE6, Firefox 2) remain required, or whether policy should target more recent browser versions while maintaining Section 508 compliance.

Data-warehouse denormalization: if a denormalized reporting schema is considered for performance, who will own ETL and data sync responsibilities and what maximum acceptable replication lag is permitted?

Clarification request for blacklisted candidates: stakeholders should review the candidate IDs listed in the blacklist and direct whether each should be (a) merged into an existing requirement above, (b) formed into a new discrete requirement, or (c) permanently discarded as out-of-scope or redundant.

candidates.name: Library Material Volume Report Capabilities
candidates.explanation: The system should be able to generate reports on the number of items in the library at any given moment, with breakdowns by categories such as total items, holds, adult fiction, and board books. It should include counts for items recently added, items on the shelf, and items checked out. The report should support filters and summaries over time, including the ability to see historical data. It should also support customizable categories.
candidates.quote:
The system should provide the ability to report on the volume of material
in a given library at any point in time, based on:
- New acquisitions
- Items on the shelf (checked in)
- Items out in circulation (checked out)

The report should allow breaking down volume in categories such as:
- Total items in library
- Number of holds
- Number of adult fiction
- Number of board books
- Other customizable categories

candidates.explanation: The system requirements include the generation of a report that, for each genre and format, displays the percentage of total circulations, the percentage of the collection, and the percentage of total shelf space. This report should be able to run per library and per system, and facilitate comparison between different libraries or branches, including side-by-side comparisons.
